title: Opal Insurance edge VPC migration and sizing playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for the Opal Insurance VPC/on-prem private deployment. Goal: propose a minimally disruptive migration path from their current hybrid infra to a Redwood Private edge deployment in their AWS accounts + on-prem training/backup nodes. This doc mixes sizing notes, Terraform module changes, an upgrade plan, and open questions for the customer call.

Status & scope:
- Draft: internal engineering playbook and customer-facing checklist.
- Scope: production inference serving (transactional chat/generation), embedding jobs, and a small eval/QA cluster for nightly regressions. Not covering data ingestion pipelines beyond basic networking/certificates.

High-level proposal:
- Primary deployment in Opal AWS VPC (us-east-2). Dedicated Redwood Private control plane endpoints hosted in Opal account (private link), serving runtime on dedicated EC2/GPU Fleet + 2 on-prem nodes for failover/large-batch offline jobs.
- Use Terraform modules from infra-registry with small Opal-specific overlays.

Assumptions (call these out to Opal):
1) Opal will provide an admin IAM role and a short-lived cross-account role for initial bootstrap (ARNs to be provided).
2) Standard VPC CIDR available: 10.44.0.0/16 (customer to confirm no conflicts).
3) KMS keys available in the account and HSM/CloudHSM options discussed — default to AWS KMS for first rollout.
4) Expected steady QPS: 30 req/s for text generation (95th p50 latency SLO 200ms token), plus 5 batch embedding jobs per hour. Peak QPS during business hours ~60 req/s.
5) Token characteristics: avg 180 generation tokens per request (used for cost sizing).
6) On-prem nodes are behind a NAT and can reach outbound endpoints for image/pull and KV-cache sync; not publicly accessible.

Sizing (initial proposal):
- Serving pool: 4x p4d.24xlarge (8x8-GPU instances) for primary capacity. Rationale: target baseline ~120 concurrent streams with token-level batching, ~2.5k tokens/sec sustained across pool.
- Canary pool: 1x g5.12xlarge (dev/QA).
- On-prem batch nodes: 2x A100 80GB boxes (rackable), used for nightly evals and heavy batched retrainable workflows.
- Control plane (in-account): 2 t3a.large for API fronting + NLB, autoscale disabled for control plane (manual failover).
- Storage: 3TB EBS gp3 per GPU instance for model shards + 10TB S3 (customer-managed) for long-term model artifacts and evaluations.
- DB/state: single Primary RDS PostgreSQL db.m6g.large (initial), encrypted with KMS. All secrets in AWS Secrets Manager.
- Network throughput: ensure ENIs sized for bursting (enhanced networking).

Quick cost note (very approximate):
- Cloud GPU hourly estimate (p4d): $~32/hr * 4 = $128/hr baseline + storage + network. This is a placeholder — finance to reconcile.

Terraform notes and module changes (engineering action items):
- Use registry modules: redwood-terraform/vpc (v1.8.0), redwood-terraform/gpu-fleet (v0.9.2). Create opal overlay module: opal-terraform/opal-edge-overlay (local).
- Required changes: add parameter enable_sg_e2e_inspection = true (Opal security requirement), add kms_key_arn input to rds and secrets modules.
- Introduce new module redwood-terraform/kv-syncer to support cross-instance KV cache persistence; upstream PR created: github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/198 (needs review).
- Plan: run terraform plan in a staging account using Opal overlay, push tfstate to customer S3 bucket with server-side encryption and DynamoDB lock table.
- Locking strategy: DynamoDB table 'opal-tf-locks' (customer to create or grant perms).

Upgrade & migration plan (3-week sprint style; milestone-driven):
Week 0 (prep):
- Confirm IAM roles, VPC CIDR, KMS key ARNs. Create Jira tasks.
- Fork Terraform overlay and deploy networking-only stack (subnets, route tables, peering). Run plan with Opal engineers present.

Week 1 (control plane & baseline infra):
- Deploy control plane (2 API nodes, secrets, RDS). Smoke test admin console behind private link.
- Validate KMS integration and key rotation policy.

Week 2 (serving pool + canary):
- Provision GPU fleet + NLB + autoscaling policies (min=2, desired=4).
- Deploy canary model and proxy rules. Run synthetic load to validate latency SLO and batching behavior.

Week 3 (cutover & rollback window):
- Gradual route traffic with 10/30/60/100% increments. Monitor token-level latency/cost in Redwood Console.
- If errors > threshold (error-rate 2% or latency > SLO for 10m) rollback to previous endpoint with traffic shift.

Post-cutover (operationalize):
- Full runbook including scaling knobs, eviction thresholds, KV cache warmup scripts, and cost dashboards. Hand-off to Opal SRE with runbook walkthrough.

Rollback & failure modes:
- TF plan can be used to destroy newly created autoscaling group and re-register old ASG. Keep AMI snapshot of previous runtime.
- If RDS upgrade causes issues, promote read replica (if configured) or restore from point-in-time snapshot — target RTO 2 hours.
- If model serving nodes exhaust GPU memory, fallback policy should route to smaller quantized model variant (configure via routing policy in route table).

Security & compliance notes:
- KMS policies must include cross-account decrypt for Redwood control plane role if we use cross-account key. Prefer customer-owned KMS with explicit access.
- Audit logs: enable VPC Flow Logs, CloudTrail, and centralized S3 bucket for logs. Retention policy 90 days initially.
- PCI/PII: Opal indicated regulated PII; ensure S3 bucket has object-level encryption and limited lifecycle.

Open questions / follow-ups for customer meeting: (mark TODO)
- Confirm exact VPC CIDR and whether Opal has existing VPC endpoints (S3, KMS) we should leverage.
- Do they require CloudHSM for KMS or is AWS KMS acceptable for Phase 1?
- Expected RPS growth in 6 months — will we need to pre-warm additional GPU capacity?
- On-prem network: can we open outbound port range 443 only, or do we need additional ports for kv-sync?
- Backup window constraints: preferred maintenance hours?

Operational play snippets (to keep handy):
- Terraform apply sequence: 1) overlay/network 2) control-plane 3) storage+secrets 4) gpu-fleet 5) models/routes 6) canary
- Canary validation script (high-level): run 1k synthetic requests over 10m with golden prompt set, assert 95p latency < 400ms and error-rate < 1.5%

Notes to implementers (short-hand):
- Keep tfstate in customer bucket; we only maintain read-only copy for audit.
- tag all infra with: owner:opal, project:opal-edge, env:prod or env:staging.
- Add telemetry exporter config to instances to forward token-level metrics to the Redwood control plane via private link.

Unresolved engineering tasks: (labelled for PRs)
- PR 198: kv-syncer terraform module (blocks: code review, unit tests).
- PR 203: patch to gpu-fleet module to support placement group affinity for on-prem interop.
- Add integration test for KMS cross-account decrypt (jira OPAL-4123).

Appendix: quick calculation used for GPU sizing (very rough):
- assumption: 1 p4d can sustain ~600 tokens/sec with optimized runtime for gen model X.
- target sustained tokens/sec: 180 tokens/request * 30 req/sec = 5400 tokens/sec => ~9 p4d equivalents => but we expect batching, caching and traffic smoothing so choose 4 p4d initial with autoscale to 8. (we'll validate in canary)
- on-prem A100 boxes for heavy offline batch: sized to run 10 concurrent 80-token-batched jobs.

Conversation history & references:
- Slack thread: #cust-opal-thread-3 (see linked artifacts) for network constraints.
- Opal requirements doc: confluence/OPAL/requirements-v1 (customer provided).

Next steps (internal owners):
- Aisha: consolidate assumptions and update overlay variables (due 2025-03-03).
- Diego: cut kv-syncer PR tests and address review comments (due 2025-03-07).
- Priya: draft security checklist and KMS policy template to share with Opal (due 2025-03-05).

Notes to self: keep this doc \"chatty\" — it's a working artifact. Remove speculative cost numbers before handing to finance. Mark final doc when customer confirms KMS and CIDR.
